AWAR D 1.
Present claim petition has been filed under Section 166/140 of M.V. Act by the petitioners being legal heirs of deceased Samshad Malik.

Facts in brief are that on 07.09.2020 at about 10.00 p.m. deceased Shamshad Malik was going towards his house at Shalimar Garden, Ghaziabad from Loni and when he reached in front of Kanchan Park, in the meanwhile a truck bearing registration no.RJ-02GB-8057 being driven by its driver in high speed and in a rash and negligent manner came and hit the deceased.
As a result of such impact, deceased sustained serious/grievous injuries and later succumbed to injuries.
Regarding the accident in question an FIR No.742/20202 under Section 279/304A IPC was registered at PS Loni, Ghaziabad, UP.
2. It is stated that deceased was aged 30 years at the time of accident and he was doing his business by which he was earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
It is stated that respondent no.1 is the driver-cum- owner of offending vehicle which was insured with respondent no.2/United India Insurance Company Limited.
3. Despite opportunities given, respondent no.1 has not filed the WS.
Therefore opportunity to file WS on behalf of respondent no.1 was closed on 31.08.2023.
4. WS was filed on behalf of respondent no.2/insurance company wherein an objection has been taken that driver was not holding valid and MACT No.180/2021 Page 2 SHELENDER by SHELENDER MALIK MALIK
Date: 2024.10.05 16:02:46 +0530 effective DL at the time of accident.

Respondent no.2 has taken the defence in terms of Section 134(c), 147, 149, 170 of M.V.
Act.
It is stated that deceased himself was moving in rash and negligent manner without holding a valid DL.
However it is admitted that the vehicle in question was insured under policy no.1417003119P113244020 with validity from 14.01.2020 to 13.01.2021.
Contents of the claim petition have been denied.
5. On the basis of pleadings of parties following issues were framed by my ld. Predecessor on 31.08.2023 :

(1)Whether respondent no.1 was driving the offending vehicle no.RJ-02GB-8057 on 07.09.2020 at about 10:00 pm at Kanchan Park within the jurisdiction of PS Loni in a rash and negligent manner and caused the death of deceased Sh.Shamshad Malik?
OPP (2)Whether
petitioners
are entitled for compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?
OPP (3)Relief.
6. After framing of issues evidence in the case was ordered to be recorded before Local Commissioner.
Before LC, petitioners have examined three witnesses.

PW1 is petitioner no.1 Shumaila Malik (widow of deceased); PW2 is Mohd. Dilshad who is stated to be an eye witness of the accident; and PW3 is Mantosh Kumar from Income Tax Office who proved ITRs of deceased.

It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others (MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012), Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

sentences.text: To prove the manner in which accident occurred, petitioners have examined PW2 Mohd. Dilshad who deposed by way of his affidavit that he witnessed the accident occurred on 07.09.2020 at about 10.00 pm near Kanchan Park, Ghaziabad, UP as he was present at the scene and observed the accident as it occurred.
Witness says that on 07.09.2020 he visited his sister's house in Iqraam Nagar, Loni, Ghaziabad and during the night he left for his home.

PW2 deposed that at about 10.00 pm when he reached near Kanchan Park, Ghaziabad, he witnessed a truck bearing registration no.RJ-02GB-8057 being driven by its driver in high speed, rashly and negligently hit a motorist riding a motor cycle bearing registration no.UP-14EH-4083.
Witness stated that he tried to chase the truck but due to its high speed he could not stop it.

Later when he returned, there was no one at the scene of accident but the bike involved in the MACT No.180/2021 Digitally signed by SHELENDER Page 4 SHELENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.10.05 16:02:59 +0530 accident was lying there.
PW2 testified that upon inquiry he learned that the person involved in the accident had been taken to hospital and later found that the person riding the bike had passed away.

PW2 says that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of truck no.RJ-02GB-8057.
11.

Though he was cross examined at length by ld. Counsel for insurance, however he remained consistent on his stand that he saw the happening of accident from his eyes.

sentences.text: PW2 stated that on 07.09.2020 accident took place opposite Prem Nagar police chowki at about 10 p.m.
At that time he was coming from Loni Tiraha and going towards Ghaziabad and truck was also coming from Loni Tiraha and going towards Tila Mod, Ghaziabad.
Witness says that motorcycle no.UP-14EH-4083 was also going from Loni Tiraha to Tila Mod side which was being driven ahead of truck.
PW2 says that he was driving his motorcycle behind the truck.
Witness further says that he had followed the offending truck and noted down its number but could not stop the same.
PW2 gave the number of offending vehicle as RJ- 02GB-8057.

Even otherwise evidence of PW2 has been duly corroborated from criminal case documents proved in the testimony of PW1 Smt.Shumaila Malik as Ex.PW1/12 including FIR, site plan, mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle and motorcycle of deceased, post mortem report of deceased, order dated 12.01.2021 of ACJM Ghaziabad by which respondent no.1 was granted bail in criminal case etc.
Report u/s 173 Cr.PC filed by the local police also shows that respondent no.1 has been prosecuted in the criminal case.
12. Testimony of PW2 who is eye witness to the accident in MACT No.180/2021 Page 5 SHELENDER by SHELENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.10.05 16:03:06 +0530

question coupled with record of criminal case in the opinion of this Tribunal is sufficient to establish that deceased died due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing registration no.RJ-02GB- 8057 being driven by respondent no.1.
Issue No.2 13.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 14.
The present case pertains to the death of deceased Shamshad Malik.

In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.

Decided on 31.10.2017,
laying down the general principles for computation of compensation in death cases.

The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"18.

Basically only three facts need to be established by the claimants for assessing compensation in the MACT No.180/2021 by SHELENDER Page 6 SHELENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.10.05 16:03:13 +0530 case of death:

(a) age of the deceased;
(b) income of the deceased; and (c) the number of dependents.
There will
be lesser need for detailed evidence.
It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balance expired which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
MACT No.180/2021 SHELENDER MALIK Page 7

MALIK Date:

5 Step-3 (Actual Calculation) The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.

The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be added."

Deduction towards Personal Living Expenses 23.
After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
Deductions out of earning of the deceased Number of dependents Where dependent is 1 Half Where the number of dependent family 1/3rd members is 2 to 3 Where the number of dependent family 1/4th members is 4 to 6 Where the number of dependent family 1/5th members exceeds 6 (six)

(1)Whether respondent no.1 was driving the offending vehicle no.RJ-02GB-8057 on 07.09.2020 at about 10:00 pm at Kanchan Park within the jurisdiction of PS Loni in a rash and negligent manner and caused the death of deceased Sh.Shamshad Malik?

are entitled for compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others (MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012), Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
10.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.
Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.
These issues to be determined by the Tribunal to arrive at the loss of dependency are:
(i) additions/ deductions to be made for arriving at the income;
(ii) the deduction to be made towards the personal living expenses of the deceased;
and iii) the multiplier to be applied with reference to the age of the deceased.
If these determinations are standardized, there will be uniformity and consistency in the decisions.
be lesser need for detailed evidence.
It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.
19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balance expired which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thus, annual income of the deceased at the time of his death is assessed to be Rs.3,13,840/- (Rs.3,14,600 - Rs.760).
Application of Multiplier 19.
As held above, deceased was 30 years of age at the time of accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
Since on the day of accident deceased was aged around 30 and was self employed,
in view of said fact this Tribunal finds that 40% of the income of deceased (aged below 40 years) has to be considered towards future prospects.
After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.
Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
Deductions out of earning of the deceased Number of dependents Where dependent is 1 Half Where the number of dependent family 1/3rd members is 2 to 3 Where the number of dependent family 1/4th members is 4 to 6 Where the number of dependent family 1/5th members exceeds 6 (six)
24.
Further, in view of recent decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case titled as United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur & Ors., Civil Appeal no. 2705 of 2020, decided on 30.06.2020, loss of consortium has to be fixed for each of the LRs.
